subject: Probe divergence during vendor maintenance — availability discrepancy
messages:
From: Elaine Morris <elaine@orchidhealth.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency spike / failed requests during provider maintenance (Jun 19 22:10-22:45 PDT)

Jordan —

We saw a spike in 5xx responses and elevated p95 latency for our inference endpoints last night between ~22:10 and 22:45 PDT. Our side-by-side dashboards (internal and Redwood) show a divergence: our edge counts show ~12% failed requests while Redwood's reported service availability was still within SLO. CDN Fast has posted a maintenance notice for 22:00-22:30 PDT (ticket 92741) and they indicate an automated POP drain.

This resulted in user-visible errors for several of our clients. Per the contract (section 3.2) we are requesting an SLA review and credit if applicable — specifically: how you are calculating partial degradations when a third-party maintenance window overlaps Redwood's probe results.

Attached are our sample error traces and the timeseries windows. Please confirm receipt and next steps.

Thanks,
Elaine Morris
Director, Platform Engineering
Orchid Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 07:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency spike / failed requests during provider maintenance (Jun 19 22:10-22:45 PDT)

Jordan / Kim —

I dug into the probe-trace logs and request sampling for ORCHID-Prod between 22:00–23:00 PDT on 2027-06-19. High-level notes:

- Our regional probe fanout was lower than expected for the west-us POPs due to a transient agent restart at 21:58 PDT; probes from those POPs resumed at 22:18 PDT. That created a visibility gap 22:00–22:18 where our native probes under-sampled the impacted POPs.
- CDN Fast's maintenance window (22:00–22:30) overlapped with our probe gap. CDN Fast confirms they drained sessions in several POPs (see support ticket 92741).
- Request logs from Orchid show elevated 5xxs between 22:10–22:35 aligned with CDN Fast drain; our edge logs also show routing sticky behavior — some sessions remained pinned to drained hosts until cache TTLs expired, prolonging errors beyond the drain period.

Given the probe gap plus vendor maintenance, I recommend a split-responsibility approach rather than full or zero credit. My suggested apportionment: Redwood 40% responsibility, CDN Fast 45%, Orchid 15% (sticky session TTLs & retry configs). I put the calculation and time-series slices in the attached CSV (SLA_calc_breakdown_Orchid_20270622.csv). Also attached the probe trace file.

Action items I propose for remediation / prevention:
- Increase probe fanout and add agent restart monitoring alerts (owner: infra).
- Implement faster session failover using shorter sticky TTLs for affected routes (owner: runtime).
- Add provider maintenance detection heuristic to surface vendor drains in the Console SLO timeline (owner: product).

Happy to present this to Elaine once we confirm math.

Marissa Cole
Senior Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Confirmed: the scheduled POP drain occurred 2027-06-19 22:00–22:30 PDT. We targeted POPs in west-us region and used a graceful drain, which unfortunately resulted in session tears for some long-lived connections. We see a minority of errors persisting to 22:36 PDT due to client-side connection stickiness. We accept partial responsibility for the drain-related errors.

Ticket: 92741 (linked above)
Regards,
CDN Fast Operations

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Morris <elaine@orchidhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, support@cdnfast.net
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Resolution proposal: partial SLA credit and next steps

Elaine —

Thank you for the data and patience while we investigated. Summary and proposed resolution:

1) Root cause summary:
- CDN Fast scheduled POP maintenance (22:00–22:30 PDT) caused a portion of the traffic to be drained.
- Redwood experienced a probe visibility gap (22:00–22:18 PDT) due to an agent restart in west-us which caused under-sampling of the affected POPs in our aggregated metric.
- Session stickiness extended error visibility beyond the drain window for some clients.

2) Apportionment and credit:
- Based on the attached breakdown (SLA_calc_breakdown_Orchid_20270622.csv) we propose a proportional credit: Redwood accepts 40% responsibility and will issue a credit equal to 40% of the prorated monthly invoice for the affected SLO bucket. CDN Fast has acknowledged partial responsibility; we will coordinate mutual remediation but cannot credit on their behalf.

3) What we will do now:
- Issue the 40% prorated credit to Orchid within the next billing cycle (Finance ref: CR-2027-0619).
- Implement the three remediation actions Marissa recommended (probe fanout alerting, shorter sticky TTL option for Orchid routes, vendor-drain detection flag).
- Provide a post-mortem note in Console and a short walkthrough of the credit calculation for your team.

If this is acceptable I will schedule the credit and send a follow-up with the exact dollar amount. If you believe the apportionment is incorrect, please let us know with any additional logs and we can re-evaluate.

Apologies for the disruption — we want to make sure you have predictable behavior going forward.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
